gates.FIT: Does the engine's own free variable/spec target the SAME mathematical object the step teaches (not a same-named-but-different quantity)?
gates.REACH: Does the step's actual numbers/claim fit inside the engine's schema range/precision/type without distortion?
gates.READOUT: Does the widget's visible/narrated state directly display the claim being taught, not something merely adjacent to it?
gates.NOVELTY: Does the learner do something in this lesson they have not already done? An interaction duplicating one the lesson already performs on the same central relationship does NOT count, even with different numbers -- this is the CCC 'does not count' case.
gates.DEMAND: Is the interaction educationally justified at all? Definitional / notational / epistemic / tool-selection questions usually are NOT -- there is no mathematical object whose STATE is in question, only a fact, a convention, or a choice of method to recall. If reading and thinking is strictly better than manipulating, REFUSE. (Precedent: SESSION208_INTEGRATION_REVIEW.md's original framing -- 'does the learner still have to SUPPLY the claim, not just have it shown' -- generalized here to cover the no-object case, not only the answer-is-printed case.)

methodology.cccNote: Causal Concept Coverage: does the learner directly manipulate the CENTRAL mathematical relationship of the concept at least once, where that relationship is inherently manipulable? A manipulative proof of a GENERAL rule (e.g. 'y=f(x)+k shifts the graph by k, for any f') covers every SPECIFIC instance of that rule (a different parent function f, different k) -- drilling the same rule on a different symbol is legitimate arithmetic practice but is NOT a second causal-coverage event, and does not count toward NOVELTY.

masteryRubric.note: The five gates are pass/fail and any single FAIL is an automatic REFUSE regardless of score, per mandate. masteryScore is a SEPARATE additive rubric for ranking candidates that clear all five gates. The rubric's exact dimension names were not fully specified in the mandate text as received by this worker (only its shape: 6 positive dimensions scored 0-3/0-3/0-3/0-3/0-2/0-2, max 16; 5 named penalties; bands P0/P1/optional/REFUSE). To keep scoring auditable rather than opaque, this worker operationalized six dimensions consistent with that shape and applied them uniformly. A different worker's dimension NAMES might differ; the arithmetic and the underlying judgment are shown so the score can be checked against the reasoning, not just trusted.

positiveDimensions_max16.causalCentrality_0to3: Does the interaction manipulate the CENTRAL relationship of the concept (CCC's core question)? 0=peripheral, 3=IS the central relationship.
positiveDimensions_max16.reachPrecision_0to3: How exactly does the engine's free variable/spec match this step's actual mathematical target? 0=forced, 3=exact native fit verified against schema.ts.
positiveDimensions_max16.readoutClarity_0to3: Does the widget's live state directly show the claim (vs. requiring inference)? 0=indirect, 3=direct.
positiveDimensions_max16.feedbackDepth_0to3: Quality of misconception-naming feedback the engine's schema fields and engine-capabilities.json err/conseq ratings support. 0=generic, 3=names the specific misconception.
positiveDimensions_max16.demandStrength_0to2: Does the learner genuinely DETERMINE/construct the answer rather than recognize or recall it? 0=recall-flavored, 2=construct-from-scratch.
positiveDimensions_max16.reuseConfidence_0to2: 0=engine has no shipped precedent anywhere relevant; 1=engine and this exact field/mode combination are machinery-proven (schema + tests + adversarial review) but have ZERO shipped authored instances; 2=this exact engine+mode configuration already has >=1 shipped authored instance in the corpus.

namedPenalties.duplicateInteractionPenalty: -3 if the proposed interaction substantially repeats one already proven in the SAME lesson on the same relationship (the CCC 'does not count' case, scored here even though it is really a NOVELTY-gate matter, to show how close a near-duplicate came).
namedPenalties.mobileErgonomicsPenalty: -2 if the engine's engine-capabilities.json 'mobile' rating is 1 (the poor tier) for this interaction shape.
namedPenalties.freshnessPenalty: -2 if the specific numeric case is a trivial cosmetic re-skin of an already-authored case with no new mathematical content.
namedPenalties.unauthoredStringsPenalty: -1 flat, acknowledging that every candidate needs several new required feedback strings authored in the lesson's own voice -- a real but small implementation cost, applied to every candidate that reaches scoring.
namedPenalties.adaptRiskPenalty: -2 if the engine's engine-capabilities.json 'adapt' rating is 0 (no proven adaptive/remedial pathway).

priorityBands.P0: masteryScore >= 12 (75% of the 16-point max) AND all five gates PASS
priorityBands.P1: masteryScore 8-11 AND all five gates PASS
priorityBands.optional: masteryScore 4-7 AND all five gates PASS
priorityBands.REFUSE: ANY gate FAILS (automatic, regardless of score), OR masteryScore < 4

masteryRubric.refuseScoringNote: Computing the full 6-dimension arithmetic for all 27 REFUSE entries below would be verbose without adding information, since one gate failure is dispositive. REFUSE entries instead carry an abbreviated holistic estimate (0-11) reflecting how close the candidate came, so a future worker can tell a near-duplicate (score ~9-11, would have been P1 but for NOVELTY) from a true gap (score ~7-9, FIT fails but the math object is real and DEMAND passes) from a no-object case (score ~1-3, both FIT and DEMAND fail).

A_duplicateInteraction_orSaturation.definition: The lesson already has >=1 proven rich manipulative (manip>=2) directly on the concept's central relationship. Remaining non-rich steps are numeric/mcq drill on the IDENTICAL relationship, sometimes with a different specific symbol or parent function but never a different relationship. Under CCC this does not count as new causal coverage, however good the arithmetic practice value. This was the single most common refusal reason this round, occurring in every one of the five prioritized courses (vectors-matrices, function-transformations, similarity, triangle-congruence, polygons-quadrilaterals) and in the two exponents-polynomials lessons checked as capability-activation support.
A_duplicateInteraction_orSaturation.keyRefinement_crossSymbolIsStillDuplicat: ft-02-01/ft-03-01/ft-03-02 establish precisely that a manipulative proof of a GENERAL transformation rule (shift/reflect/stretch) using ONE parent function covers every other parent function's instance of that same rule. Testing y=sqrt(x)+3 after only ever manipulating y=x^2+k is not new causal coverage -- the rule, not the symbol, is the central relationship.
A_duplicateInteraction_orSaturation.guidanceForFutureWorkers: Before adjudicating a non-rich step, first check whether ANY step in the same lesson already carries a manip>=2 widget on the same conceptTag family. If yes, treat every other non-rich step as presumptively REFUSE on NOVELTY unless it demonstrably manipulates a DIFFERENT relationship (e.g. pq-05-03's i1-certify vs i2-recall split, or vec-03-02's zero-vs-nonzero-target distinction, which is why that one entry escaped this pattern, if only barely).

B_noMathematicalObject_orDemandFail.definition: The step asks a definitional, notational, epistemic, hierarchy-recall, or theorem-consequence-recall question. There is no quantity whose STATE is in question -- only a fact, a logical relationship between statements, or a convention -- so no control surface could represent it. This is a DEMAND-gate refusal (and usually also a FIT refusal, since FIT presupposes an object to fit an engine to), not a missing-engine gap. No engine should be built for these, on principle.
B_noMathematicalObject_orDemandFail.subPattern_certifyVsRecall: pq-05-03 shows a fine-grained version of this pattern within one lesson: i1 (certify a name from markings) is genuine construction and PASSES; i2 (given the certified name, recall the theorem it unlocks) is recognition and FAILS. The same lesson can have both a good candidate and a clean refusal one step apart -- do not refuse or pass a whole lesson uniformly by topic.
B_noMathematicalObject_orDemandFail.priorCatalogueReference: Same pattern as S209's gf-01-03, cp-04-01, si-05-01, and the tool-selection half of rt-05-04 (SESSION209_RICH_MIX_ADJUDICATION.md section 2, entries 10/11/13/18).

systemsExploreEditableLines.nomination: se-01-03 (One, None, or Infinitely Many), step i1
systemsExploreEditableLines.why: This is, by the design documentation's own account, the lesson the editable-lines capability was built for. docs/RSG_DECISIONS.md states verbatim: 'The lesson the whole line-pair thread was built for now exists on a surface... Breaking a solution and repairing it is how a learner finds out what the solution WAS.' The lesson's entire content (six of seven interactive/check steps, i1 through ch1) is classification of static line pairs into one/none/infinity by comparing slope and intercept -- exactly the round trip (unique -> parallel -> coincident -> unique) the capability's own S212 landing notes describe as its motivating demonstration. This ALSO supersedes this worker's own S209 refusal of this identical step, which failed specifically because 'systemsExplore requires dragging a point to a single intersection -- it cannot represent no solution or infinitely many' -- exactly the limitation S212's editable-lines work removed.
systemsExploreEditableLines.mathematics: Line 1 fixed at y=2x+1 (m1=2,b1=1). Line 2 starts at y=3x-1 (m2=3,b2=-1; crossing at (2,5), matching the currently-authored prompt's own numbers). Dragging line 2's slope from 3 down to 2 (intercept still -1) makes the pair PARALLEL (equal slopes, different intercepts -- no solution). Further dragging the intercept from -1 up to 1 (matching line 1's b=1) makes the pair COINCIDENT (equal slopes and intercepts -- infinitely many). Dragging either back reproduces the original unique solution. All three of c1's named cases become one continuous, learner-driven demonstration instead of three separate static mcq examples scattered across i1/k1/i2.

specSketch.prompt: Line 1 is fixed at y = 2x + 1. Drag line 2 (starting at y = 3x - 1) until the system has no solution -- then find where it has infinitely many.
specSketch.successFeedback: AUTHOR -- the point sits on the original crossing (2,5)
specSketch.degenerateSystemFeedback: AUTHOR -- REQUIRED by validation whenever editLine1/editLine2 is set; must name BOTH the parallel state (no solution) and the coincident state (infinitely many) since both are reachable from this one spec

implementationNotes: xStart/yStart are set to (2,5), the pair's ORIGINAL crossing, so the point begins already correctly placed -- the task becomes purely about breaking and repairing the system, not about first hunting for a starting intersection.

One open design question, deliberately left for the implementor rather than resolved here: systemsExplore's point-placement grading (successFeedback/offLine1Feedback/offLine2Feedback) stays active alongside line-editing, so the prompt's phrasing needs to sequence 'confirm the crossing, then break it' clearly, or the point and line objectives could read as competing instructions. This is a copy/sequencing decision, not a schema limitation -- degenerateSystemFeedback already exists specifically to override point-grading language once the system goes degenerate.

editLine2's ranges were chosen so BOTH target states (slope=2 for parallel, intercept=1 for coincident) land on the authored lattice (step=1) well inside the range -- verified by hand against systemsExploreEditErrors's own start-in-range/on-lattice checks in schema.ts.

An alternative implementation could make BOTH lines editable (editLine1 and editLine2) for a fully symmetric exploration; this sketch keeps line 1 fixed to match the lesson's own established framing ('Line 1 is fixed') and to minimize first-use scope.

summary.passRate: 4/30 is loose framing -- more precisely, 4 candidates cleared all five gates (3 at P0, 1 at P1) out of 30 rigorously adjudicated this round: roughly 13%.
honestyOverYield: The P0 pool is small (3) and this is the correct, not a disappointing, outcome. The mandate explicitly asked this round to prioritize partially-rich lessons in five named courses over the 0%-rich/MCQ-heavy bucket S209 showed was low-yield (~9%). This round's finding is that the partially-rich bucket is ALSO heavily saturated, just for a different structural reason: rather than lacking a fitting engine (the 0%-rich bucket's problem), these lessons overwhelmingly follow a deliberate one-manipulative-per-lesson authoring pattern where a single rich step already proves the lesson's central relationship, and every other step is legitimate but non-novel arithmetic drill on that same relationship (pattern A above, found in 16 of this round's 26 refusals). This is arguably GOOD content design being correctly recognized, not a search failure -- but it does mean the partially-rich bucket cannot supply 45-60 more insertions either, at least not at this gate discipline.

Combined with S209 (2/22 genuine passes from the 0%-rich bucket) and this round (4/31, mostly from a targeted capability sweep rather than the prioritized bucket itself), the honest running total across both adjudication sessions is 6 genuine passes from 53 rigorous adjudications -- about 11%, and BOTH sessions' passes cluster around specific structural opportunities (a near-miss REACH failure that a new engine feature just fixed; a brand-new engine capability with zero authored users yet; a genuinely fresh mathematical case within an otherwise-covered lesson) rather than a generic 'sweep more lessons and the rate holds' pattern. (22 + 30 = 52 total adjudications across both sessions, 6 passes, ~11.5%.)

The two P0 capability-activation candidates (ep-04-02/k3, se-01-03/i1) are the strongest finds of this round specifically BECAUSE they exploit brand-new, zero-authored-user engine capabilities rather than re-treading already-covered ground -- this is likely the highest-leverage remaining lever for the insertion target: every other lesson that already has one proven manipulative is a weak target BY CONSTRUCTION, but the two new capabilities have not yet touched a single lesson, so a systematic sweep for OTHER lessons whose central relationship specifically matches area-mode factoring/distributing or breakable two-line systems (not just these two nominated ones) is likely to out-yield further sweeps of already-partially-rich lessons in the five named courses.

pq-05-03/i1 is included as a strong P0 despite coming from the DE-prioritized 0%-rich bucket -- flagged honestly in its own entry -- because it scored well on genuine merits (proven in-course engine, exact REACH match) once found via the broader sweep; it is presented as a real find, not padding.

vec-03-02/k1 is presented at P1, not P0, specifically because it is the round's clearest same-lesson near-duplicate that still narrowly clears NOVELTY -- included for completeness and because it is genuinely defensible, not because the P0 pool needed padding to 4.
